en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Ārāmavagga 57.
The Training Rule on Invitation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī.
Those bhikkhunīs said this to the other bhikkhunīs:
"Where, venerable ladies, did you complete the rains residence?"
“Where has the Saṅgha of bhikkhus performed the invitation ceremony?
“We do not invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, noble lady.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... they complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“How can it be that the bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains residence, do not invite criticism from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?
… [as before] … “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains residence, do not invite criticism from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can these bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains residence, not invite criticism from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of confidence in those who have it…” [and so forth].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:

“Whatever nun, having completed the rains residence, does not invite criticism from both Saṅghas on three grounds—either by what has been seen, or by what has been heard, or by suspicion—commits an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya). “Whatever nun”:
[as explained previously].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
"Those who have completed the rains residence" means those who have stayed for either the first three months or the last three months.

"I will not invite both Saṅghas by means of these three grounds: what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected"—by the mere act of making this resolve, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense if there is an obstacle,
or if one does not obtain it after having searched for it.
For one who is ill,
in times of distress,
for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first-time offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
